title: Numbers With a Successor

concept.title: Ask the set about the neighbour value
body: A number `x` has a **successor** in the array if `x + 1` is also in the array. Put all the numbers into a set once. Then every question "is `x + 1` present?" is answered in O(1).

body.code:
present = set(a)
count = sum(1 for x in a if x + 1 in present)

body: Note that you count **elements**, not different values: a value that occurs three times and has a successor contributes 3.

statement: Count the elements `x` of the array for which `x + 1` also occurs somewhere in the array. Equal elements are counted separately.

examples.note: Only 5 has a successor (6): the answer is 1.
1 and 2 each have a successor; the two 3s do not.

hints: Put all numbers into a set.
For each element, check whether `x + 1` is in the set.
Count the elements, so equal elements are counted each time.

explanation: A set of all values answers each "is x + 1 present?" question in O(1).
solution.complexity: Time O(n) on average, space O(n).

code.python:
import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

n = int(input())
a = list(map(int, input().split()))

present = set(a)
count = 0
for x in a:
    if x + 1 in present:
        count += 1
print(count)
